about: A Zork-like underground empire presented as a final test. You wake at the bottom of an endless stair and are told to seek an old man when you feel worthy. You fight a hooded double of yourself, cross a freezing lake, and look for a way deeper while grues kill you in the dark.

done.why: I died to grues a third time after smashing my only lamp. The world sent me to a Void and said nothing further would happen.

ending.what: A losing ending. After the third death the old man said it was perhaps another he had been seeking, and I was left in the Void.

moments.note: The Elvish sword appeared in my hand and glowed when the hooded figure showed up.
The beaten figure lowered its head and offered its hood. Removing it showed my own face, which then aged.
Swimming the lake dropped the torch I had just taken, and it went out for good.
Saying hello sailor got a gift from the old sailor.
Throwing the lamp across the lake smashed it, and I had no light for the rest of the game.
I got through the dark passage to a Key Room with a key and a manhole.
The broken lantern came back with me after respawn, so I had no light, and every dark step risked a grue.

wished: A way to carry light across the lake, or a warning that throwing the lamp would break it.
A way to use the key on the chest and get through the manhole.
A clearer warning that death scatters my items.

lines.line: Who do you think you are? Arthur?
lines.why: A funny refusal when I tried to take the sword from the rock.

lines.line: You slowly remove the hood from your badly wounded opponent and recoil in horror at the sight of your own face, weary and wounded.
lines.why: The best moment: the duel turns out to be against yourself.

lines.line: Nothing further will happen to you in this game; whoever the old man was waiting for, he has gone to look for them elsewhere.
lines.why: The closing line after the third death.

fun.why: The duel and the sailor were fun. Losing my light to the lake and then to a thrown lamp was punishing.

engagement.why: I had a clear goal of getting deeper, and each area gave me something to chase.

difficulty.why: Light, the lake and the grues combined harshly, and three deaths ended the game.

interestingness.why: Familiar Zork-style puzzles, plus new touches such as the self-duel and a lake that takes your things.

prose.why: Evocative descriptions, and the lake warning was a good hint written as atmosphere.
